title: Getting started with NICHESv2
text: create_NICHESObject() needs three things: gene--cell expression matrix, cell metadata, LR database. bundled NICHESv2_inputs list holds three, 50 genes 80 cells. column names matrix must match row names metadata. Spatial mode needs x y columns metadata.
code: data(NICHESv2_inputs) names(NICHESv2_inputs) #> [1] "count.mtx" "meta.data" "LRM.db"  dim(NICHESv2_inputs$count.mtx) #> [1] 50 80 head(NICHESv2_inputs$meta.data, 3) head(NICHESv2_inputs$LRM.db, 3)

title: Getting started with NICHESv2
text: cell connected spatial neighbors using k = 5. mutual nearest neighbors become edges, every cell also gets self-loop autocrine signaling. edge one directed cell pair. method = "product" multiplies sender’s ligand expression receiver’s receptor expression, "minimum" takes smaller two. use fixed radius instead k, pass rad; Explore_Radius_Neighborhood() helps choose value. larger datasets, set n.cores score LR pairs parallel. uses socket clusters, works every platform.
code: obj <- create_NICHESObject(   count.mtx = NICHESv2_inputs$count.mtx,   meta.data = NICHESv2_inputs$meta.data,   LRM.db    = NICHESv2_inputs$LRM.db,   mode      = "spatial",   k         = 5L,   method    = "product",   verbose   = FALSE ) dim(obj) #> cells genes edges  LRMs  #>    80    50   354    15

Edge IDs form "SendingCell|ReceivingCell" LRM IDs form "ligand|receptor". $edge.data data.table, can summarize directly. strongest LR pairs overall: $edge.meta carries cell’s metadata onto edges, Sending. text: cell’s neighborhood filled object built. aggregate_NICHESObject() summarizes one per LRM, cell.type.col also reports cell types surround cell. $aggregations$neighborhood.edge.agg one row per (cell, LRM). sorts neighborhood edge five categories relative focal cell: , , cross (two neighbors), self.autocrine .autocrine. $aggregations$neighborhood.composition one row per cell:
code: obj <- aggregate_NICHESObject(obj, cell.type.col = "celltype", verbose = FALSE) names(obj$aggregations) #> [1] "neighborhood.edge.agg"    "neighborhood.composition" agg <- obj$aggregations$neighborhood.edge.agg agg[, .(cell, LRM, score.in.sum, score.out.sum, score.cross.sum)][1:3] comp <- obj$aggregations$neighborhood.composition comp[, .(cell, TypeA.neighbor.prop, TypeB.neighbor.prop, TypeC.neighbor.prop)][1:3]

title: Getting started with NICHESv2
text: Aggregate first, subset. retained cell keeps neighborhood entries aggregation rows unchanged, values still describe whole neighborhood full tissue, including neighbors didn’t keep. edge slots subset hold edges retained cells. Summing cell’s rows sub$edge.data can therefore give less aggregation row. removed edges gone, aggregations can’t recomputed subset, trying stops error. analyze subset separate tissue, rebuild neighborhoods first:
code: type.a <- obj$cell.meta[celltype == "TypeA", cell] sub <- obj[type.a] dim(sub) #> cells genes edges  LRMs  #>    30    50   132    15  identical(   sub$aggregations$neighborhood.edge.agg[, score.in.sum],   agg[cell %in% type.a, score.in.sum] ) #> [1] TRUE separate <- add_neighborhoods(sub, overwrite = TRUE, verbose = FALSE) separate <- aggregate_NICHESObject(separate, verbose = FALSE)

title: Neighborhood aggregation
text: Aggregate full object first, subset. Neighborhood slots aggregation tables indexed cell, kept cell keeps rows unchanged. values still describe cell’s whole neighborhood, including neighbors didn’t keep. edge slots subset keep edges kept cells. Two things follow: Summing cell’s rows sub$edge.data can give less aggregation row. TissuePlex export subset shows kept edges.

title: Neighborhood aggregation
text: removed edges gone, subset can’t recompute full-tissue values, trying stops error: kept cell already correct values, rarely need recalculate. treat subset separate tissue instead, rebuild neighborhoods first. clears carried-tables, new values use kept cells:
code: add_neighborhood_edge_agg(sub, verbose = FALSE) #> Error: #> ! [add_neighborhood_edge_agg] This object is a subset whose neighborhoods include edges to removed cells, so aggregations cannot be recomputed on it. Aggregate the full object before subsetting (the results carry over), or run add_neighborhoods(obj, overwrite = TRUE) first to analyze the subset as a separate tissue. separate <- add_neighborhoods(sub, overwrite = TRUE, verbose = FALSE) separate <- aggregate_NICHESObject(separate, verbose = FALSE)

Row names = gene symbols; column names = cell barcodes. name sets must match rownames(meta.data) columns LRM.db respectively. meta.data data.frame row names = cell barcodes. Must contain x y columns mode = "spatial", column named cell.type.col mode = "nonspatial". LRM.db Either character string naming built-database ("connectomedb2025", "fantom5" "omnipath") data.frame least columns named ligand.col receptor.col. See load_LRM_database details supported species. mode Character. "spatial" (default, kNN/radius edges) "nonspatial" (type-stratified random sampling). species Species built-LRM databases. One "human" (default), "mouse", "rat", "pig" ("pig" available OmniPath). Silently ignored LRM.db data.frame. sample.col Character NULL (default). Name column meta.data identifying biological sample origin cell. supplied, pipeline runs independently within sample per-sample objects merged. See Sample-aware processing section barcode-uniqueness requirement. cell.type.col Character NULL. Column meta.data holding cell type labels. Required mode = "nonspatial"; ignored otherwise. ligand.col Character. Column name ligands LRM.db. Default "ligand". receptor.col Character. Column name receptors LRM.db. Default "receptor". k Integer NULL. Number nearest neighbors kNN edges. Spatial mode ; supply exactly one k rad. rad Numeric NULL. Neighborhood radius fixed-radius edges (units x/y columns). Spatial mode ; supply exactly one k rad. Use Explore_Radius_Neighborhood choose sensible value. seed Integer. Random seed reproducible type-stratified sampling. Default 42L. Nonspatial mode . max.cells Integer NULL. Per cell-type-pair edge cap. Default NULL (cap). Nonspatial mode . method Per-edge LR scoring method. title: Create a NICHESObject from Single-Cell Data — create_NICHESObject
text: Internally, create_NICHESObject() chains following steps: Load LR database (load_LRM_database)         LRM.db character string; otherwise supplied         data.frame used directly. Build edge list – create_Edgelist_Spatial         mode = "spatial" create_Edgelist_SamplingByType         mode = "nonspatial". Score every edge x LRM combination via         compute_CellToCell, sparsifying goes. Assemble 15-slot NICHESObject (cell, edge, gene, LRM,         segmentation, aggregation slots). Extract neighborhoods via add_neighborhoods using         edge.filter.mode = "both_in_neighborhood"         remove.autocrine = FALSE (fixed design). step also exported individually users need finer control.

title: Create a NICHESObject from Single-Cell Data — create_NICHESObject
text: sample.col supplied, meta.data split column full pipeline runs independently within sample. Per-sample objects combined via merge_NICHESObjects. prevents physically meaningless cross-sample edges (kNN search coordinates pooled across slides happily connect cells never tissue). Barcodes must globally unique across samples. duplicate barcode hard error merge step. Prepend sample-specific prefix construction (e.g.\ paste0(sample.id, "_", barcode), Seurat::RenameCells() automatically). Outer iteration samples always sequential; inner pipeline uses n.cores parallelism, socket clusters never nested.
